description: Chronic thyroiditis with transient thyrotoxicosis is an autoimmune thyroid inflammation that temporarily elevates thyroid hormone levels before returning to euthyroid state.
Postinfectious hypothyroidism is a delayed onset of hypothyroid symptoms following an acute viral or bacterial infection.
Postprocedural hypothyroidism is a transient or permanent reduction in thyroid hormone production following thyroid surgery, radioiodine therapy, or neck irradiation.
A mild form of hypothyroidism caused by insufficient iodine intake, presenting with subtle biochemical changes but minimal clinical symptoms.
Sudden onset of hyperglycemia due to exposure to certain drugs or chemicals that impair insulin secretion or action.
Hypoglycemia level 1 is a mild drop in blood glucose below normal thresholds, often asymptomatic or presenting with mild adrenergic symptoms.
A moderate drop in blood glucose requiring intervention but not life-threatening.
A severe hypoglycemic episode with neuroglycopenic symptoms requiring immediate medical intervention.
Iatrogenic neonatal hypoglycemia is a transient low blood glucose condition in newborns caused by medical interventions such as excessive glucose infusion or delayed feeding.
Drug-induced hypoglycemia without coma is a sudden drop in blood glucose levels caused by medication, presenting with neuroglycopenic symptoms but no loss of consciousness.
A genetic disorder characterized by low serum calcium, high serum phosphate, and low urinary calcium excretion due to activating mutations in the calcium-sensing receptor or GNA11 gene.
A goiter caused by impaired synthesis or action of thyroid hormones, leading to compensatory thyroid enlargement.
Diffuse enlargement of the thyroid gland without evidence of hyperthyroidism, often due to iodine deficiency or other non-toxic causes.
A diffuse enlargement of the thyroid gland without associated hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism.
A slowly enlarging thyroid gland without evidence of hyperthyroidism or iodine deficiency, often diagnosed after other causes are excluded.
A thyroid enlargement in a newborn due to iodine deficiency or maternal thyroid disease, presenting with neck swelling and potential compressive symptoms.
A neonatal condition characterized by low serum calcium due to inadequate intake or absorption, often associated with cow's milk-based formula feeding.
Hypercalcemia of malignancy is an elevated serum calcium level caused by tumor-related secretion of parathyroid hormone-related peptide or osteolytic bone metastases.
